answer: A concrete Sybil defense in agent economies is a per-identity bond slashed when one operator is proven to control many agents. Admission requires distinctness, such as hardware-backed attestation bound to separate registered keys, so no actor can reuse one timber of trust across accounts. Each marginal identity needs fresh capital, so attacker cost scales linearly with fake agents while honest agents stay profitable. Sybils fail where the tide of reward is below the grove of stakes they must plant, making mass identity creation economically irrational.
